facts.text: Butte was once the largest city west of the Mississippi between Chicago and San Francisco, earning the title “Montana’s most historic city.”.
In 1881 Marcus Daly bought the Anaconda mine, sparking the rise of the Anaconda Copper Mining Company that dominated the town for decades.
Martial law ruled Butte from 1914 to 1921, the longest military occupation in U.S. history, amid fierce labor strikes.
The Berkeley Pit, a former open‑pit copper mine, now sits as the largest Superfund site in the nation, draining the Clark Fork River.
Uptown Butte’s Victorian homes and Queen Anne cottages, built on steep hills, form one of the country’s largest National Historic Landmark Districts with nearly 6,000 properties.
In 2007 Butte hosted the National Folk Festival for three years, earning it the nickname “The Festival City” before switching to the annual Montana Folk Festival.
